newsitem.title: USA: Northeastern U.S. daily power mixed as temps ease.
newsitem.headline: Northeastern U.S. daily power mixed as temps ease.

text.p: Day-ahead electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. bulk market traded mixed Thursday as frigid temperatures were forecast to moderate over the next couple of days.

Temperatures in the Northeast were predicted to average near five degrees F below normal Friday and Saturday with a chance of rain, to be followed by a steep drop to 10-17 degrees below normal Sunday.
"The worst of it was last night," said a Northeast power trader, adding spot supplies to New England from Quebec were reduced today due to high demand in the Canadian province.
But the situation did not have a noticeable effect on next-day prices in the region.
"It has more to do with pool resources. I didn't see much change," said another trader in the Northeast.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Friday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border (including transmission costs) was quoted again at $33.00-$35.00 per Megawatt hour (MWh).
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery at the NU border held at $28.00.
Spot power availability in New York improved today as the 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick plant ramped toward full output.

The Scriba, N.Y., station reached 50 percent power output today after it was taken off line last week to remove fish and debris clogging screens on the intakes that bring cooling water into the plant.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Friday delivery in the eastern half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) stepped down to $31.00-$32.00 MWh from Wednesday's $32.50-$33.50.
Off-peak, non-firm power for day-ahead delivery in eastern NYPP stayed in a $22.00-$24.00 range.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Friday tightened to $28.00-$29.00 from Wednesday's $27.00-$29.00.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday continued to hold at $17.50-$18.50.

The two units at the Indian Point nuclear generating complex north of New York City remained shut. The 975 MW unit 2, which was shut January 18 to correct problems with a feedwater valve, will likely restart next week. The 965 MW unit 3 was expected to stay idled through mid-February for replacement work in its primary containment area.
Swing natural gas values at the New York City gate were weaker, quoted at $3.60-$3.80 per million British thermal units compared with Wednesday's $3.70-$4.00.
